findings.reason: the fix should extend the existing stranded-launch release to the plan branch (or name why it cannot), rather than design a second release; the plan's own done-when only asks for the step to be named, which would produce a parallel mechanism.
findings.text: §16 proposes a plan-review pointer fix without citing the stranded-launch release that already exists and already runs for the non-plan review branch: `_standing_plan_review` + the plan branch at `dispatch_review_for_run` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:2324`) never call `_stranded_launch`/`_discard_stranded_review`, while the non-plan branch does so at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:2402`, and `_stranded_launch` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:6613`) already classifies exactly the observed pidless `starting` pointer, its own action text asserting "a review it claimed is released by the reflex" — a claim false for the plan path

findings.reason: the plan must state whether `RECKON_FLEET_RECORD` is retired into `FLEET_STATE_DIR` (migrating those callers) or retained, otherwise the named owner is not a superset of the resolver it replaces and dispatch stops reading records those tests publish.
findings.text: §18 resolves the fleet record through `fleet_supervisor.state_directory` but leaves the second resolver's other override unaccounted: `_fleet_record_path` today also honours `RECKON_FLEET_RECORD` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:9640`) and `XDG_STATE_HOME`, neither of which `state_directory` reads, and four test files set `RECKON_FLEET_RECORD`

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan already carries §17, which folds the per-run supervisor's spread of private helpers in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` (12,672 lines: `_supervisor...`/`_supervisor_spec`/`_start_supervisor`/`_supervisor_command`) behind a module boundary; §10's `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py` is itself a deep module hiding the FIFO protocol, runtime directory and verbs behind its `main`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 names `fleet_supervisor.state_directory` (`reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:253`) as the owner to extend, but that owner does not cover the second resolver's other override, `RECKON_FLEET_RECORD` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:9640`), which four test files set.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; none of the implementable sections (§15, §16, §17, §18) adds a CLI option or an MCP view, and §8 already names the one refusal it retires (the `max_concurrent_runs` roster bound), so no section adds to a family without accounting for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §16 designs a release for a plan-review pointer stranded before launch without citing the release machinery the sibling non-plan branch already uses (`_stranded_launch` at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:6613` and `_discard_stranded_review` at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:1342`, applied at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:2402`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — each added layer (the FIFO `spawn` verb, `reckon/crew/supervisor_main.py`, `supervised_launch`) sits over machinery §10 and §17 name, and §17 folds the thin `supervisor_main` wrapper into the supervisor's own module; no wrapper is added over an extendable owner without a stated reason.
